questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a primary goal of an operating system?
o: Compiling source code into machine code
questions.e: Compiling source code is the job of a compiler, not the operating system. The OS manages hardware resources, provides user interfaces, and ensures fair resource allocation among processes.

questions.q: The kernel is the core component of an operating system that manages system resources and provides basic services.
questions.e: This statement is TRUE. The kernel is indeed the core component that manages CPU scheduling, memory management, file systems, and other essential system resources.

questions.q: In a multiprogramming system, what is the primary reason for keeping multiple programs in memory simultaneously?
questions.e: Multiprogramming keeps multiple programs in memory to maximize CPU utilization. When one program is waiting for I/O, the CPU can switch to execute another program, reducing idle time.

questions.q: Which type of storage is the fastest but also the most expensive per byte?
questions.e: CPU registers are the fastest storage in the memory hierarchy but also the most expensive per byte. They provide immediate access to data for the CPU but are limited in capacity.

questions.q: In a time-sharing system, each user has the illusion of having the entire computer to themselves.
questions.e: TRUE. Time-sharing systems switch between users so quickly that each user feels they have exclusive access to the system, even though resources are actually being shared.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of system calls?
o: To call functions within the same program
To provide an interface between user programs and the operating system
questions.e: System calls provide the interface between user programs and the OS kernel, allowing programs to request services like file operations, process control, and memory management from the operating system.

questions.q: User mode has restricted access to system resources and cannot execute privileged instructions.
questions.e: TRUE. User mode is designed to protect the system by restricting access to critical resources and privileged instructions. Only kernel mode can execute privileged operations.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the concept of spooling?
o: Direct communication between CPU and I/O devices
Simultaneous peripheral operations online using buffers
A method for compressing data in memory
A technique for encrypting system files
questions.e: Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line) uses buffers to hold data for devices like printers, allowing the CPU to continue processing while I/O operations occur in the background.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using virtual machines?
o: They are faster than physical machines
They provide complete isolation between different OS environments
They require less memory than regular programs
They eliminate the need for device drivers
questions.e: Virtual machines provide complete isolation between different OS environments, allowing multiple operating systems to run on the same physical hardware safely and independently.

questions.q: Cache memory is used to speed up access to frequently used data by storing copies closer to the CPU.
questions.e: TRUE. Cache memory is a smaller, faster memory that stores copies of frequently accessed data from main memory, reducing access time for the CPU.

questions.q: Which component is responsible for selecting the next process to run on the CPU?
questions.e: The scheduler selects which process should run next based on the scheduling algorithm. The dispatcher then performs the actual context switch to give control to the selected process.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a program and a process?
o: A program is written in high-level language, a process is in machine code
A program is passive (on disk), a process is active (in execution)
A program can only run on one CPU, a process can run on multiple CPUs
There is no difference, they are the same thing
questions.e: A program is a passive entity stored on disk (executable file), while a process is an active entity - a program in execution with associated resources like memory, CPU state, and open files.

questions.q: Real-time operating systems guarantee that critical tasks will be completed within specified time constraints.
questions.e: TRUE. Real-time operating systems are designed specifically to guarantee that time-critical tasks meet their deadlines. Hard real-time systems provide absolute guarantees, while soft real-time systems provide strong scheduling preferences.
